name: umoya-sj-chapters
title: SJ Journey Chapters
description: The three chapters: History & Culture, Safari, The Cape.

controls.label: Text 3
controls.default: Where the country's recent history is closest to the surface, and its creative present most alive. You begin with a warm welcome, then spend a full day in Soweto with the township's own people, before standing where the story of freedom was written.

controls.label: Alt Text
controls.default: Johannesburg and Soweto — history and culture

controls.label: Text 2
controls.default: Into the iconic safari country of the lowveld. Three nights at MalaMala, a private Big Five reserve returned to the community that lives there, with open-vehicle game drives morning and evening, and an afternoon given to the people whose home this land is.

controls.label: Alt Text
controls.default: Open-vehicle game drive in the Sabi Sand

controls.label: Text 3
controls.default: The journey closes where the land meets two oceans. Robben Island and Table Mountain, the Cape Peninsula, a day among the Black-owned wineries of the Cape, and a farewell worthy of the journey behind it.

controls.label: Alt Text
controls.default: Cape Town — where the land meets two oceans

rows.alt: A welcome dinner hosted by the winemaker behind Luc Mo
rows.mom_desc: A welcome dinner hosted by the winemaker behind Luc Mo, built with the Ndebele Kingdom.
A full day through Soweto by tuk-tuk, with local guides, and lunch hosted by the sister of Hector Pieterson.

rows.mom_desc: The places where the struggle was lived, told plainly and with care.

controls.label: Description

rows.alt: Big Five game drive in the Sabi Sand
rows.mom_desc: Morning and evening in open vehicles with private field guides, unhurried and close.

rows.alt: MalaMala, the community-owned reserve in the Sabi Sand
rows.mom_desc: MalaMala was taken from its community during apartheid. Through decades of determination, they fought for it, won it back, and today they welcome you onto it.

rows.alt: A Shangaan village, the community beyond the reserve
rows.mom_desc: Time with the community that lives alongside the wilderness.

controls.label: Description
controls.default: The warder who guarded Nelson Mandela, and became his friend, walks you through himself.

rows.mom_desc: The warder who guarded Nelson Mandela, and became his friend, walks you through himself.

rows.alt: Black-owned wineries of the Cape Winelands
rows.mom_desc: A day among Black-owned wineries, with the CEO of Seven Sisters Vineyards, a pioneer who established the prominent, 100% black-owned wine brand in Stellenbosch.
